definitions.explanation: The overall visual appearance of an area, especially as shaped by natural features, architecture, and urban planning. Often used in contexts involving preservation and regulation of the visual environment.

examples.japanese: この{町|まち}は{景観|けいかん}が{美|うつく}しい。
{景観|けいかん}を{守|まも}るために{建物|たてもの}の{高|たか}さが{制限|せいげん}されている。
examples.english: Building height is restricted to preserve the landscape.

examples.japanese: {歴史的|れきしてき}な{景観|けいかん}を{損|そこ}なわないよう、{新|あたら}しい{建築|けんちく}には{厳|きび}しい{基準|きじゅん}が{設|もう}けられている。
examples.english: Strict standards have been established for new construction so as not to spoil the historical landscape.

notes:
USAGE:
More formal and specific than {景色|けしき} (scenery). {景観|けいかん} emphasizes the overall visual character of an area, especially in the context of urban planning, architecture, and environmental protection. Japan has a {景観法|けいかんほう} (Landscape Act) that regulates development to preserve scenic areas.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {景観|けいかん}を{守|まも}る: to protect the landscape
- {景観|けいかん}を{損|そこ}なう: to spoil the landscape
- {景観|けいかん}{条例|じょうれい}: landscape ordinance
- {自然|しぜん}{景観|けいかん}: natural landscape
- {都市|とし}{景観|けいかん}: urban landscape

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {景色|けしき}: scenery, view (everyday, general)
- {風景|ふうけい}: scenery, landscape (literary, often visual art)
- {眺|なが}め: view (from a specific vantage point)
